body:
## Linked issue

Closes #326

## What changed

Added `test_no_hand_rolled_message_nodes_ddl_in_tests` to `tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py`. It walks the AST of every `tests/*.py` file (excluding the blessed `tests/_sessions_db_fixtures.py` helper) and matches a whitespace-spanning DDL pattern (`CREATE\s+TABLE(\s+IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS)?\s+message_nodes\b`, case-insensitive) against the *full value* of every string constant in the file — not a per-line scan. A plain `ast.Constant` visit already reaches f-string literal segments and docstrings, since both are `Constant` nodes in the tree, so no special-casing is needed for those. The failure message reports the offending file and the literal node's line number, and points offenders to `make_sessions_db` in the shared helper.

**Rework (this push):** the original version scanned `splitlines()` per line, which meant a hand-rolled DDL wrapped across lines inside one string literal (e.g. `"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS\nmessage_nodes ("`) was never detected — mutation-proven false negative flagged in review. Replaced with the AST walk described above, per the #323 / `test_load_state_locked.py:165-196` precedent the issue named. Also folded in the two optional nits: a `\b` word boundary after `message_nodes` (so `message_nodes_archive` doesn't false-positive), and a guarded UTF-8 read so a non-UTF-8 test file fails cleanly, naming the file instead of an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError`.

The two intentional `CREATE TABLE sessions` malformed-schema regression tests (`test_worktree.py` and `test_post_mortem.py`) are left untouched and remain green.

## Verification

All evidence below was collected against the pushed head, using an isolated `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` (never `--active`, never a bare `uv sync` inside the worktree).

**1. Baseline — no mutation, blessed source unaffected:**
```
uv run pytest -q --tb=short tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py -v
2 passed in 0.30s
```

**2. Single-line mutation** (`HAND_ROLLED = "CREATE TABLE message_nodes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)"`) **and 3. multi-line mutation** (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / newline / `message_nodes (` inside one triple-quoted string) added as temp files and run together — the guard now catches both, including the one the old per-line scan missed:
```
uv run pytest -q --tb=short tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py::test_no_hand_rolled_message_nodes_ddl_in_tests

AssertionError: Hand-rolled message_nodes DDL found in tests. Use _sessions_db_fixtures.make_sessions_db instead:
  tests\test_zzz_mutation_multiline.py:1: 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS message_nodes ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY )'
  tests\test_zzz_mutation_singleline.py:1: 'CREATE TABLE message_nodes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)'
```

**4. Word-boundary control** (`HAND_ROLLED = "CREATE TABLE message_nodes_archive (x INT)"`) — not flagged in the run above (only the two real offenders appear), and confirmed in isolation:
```
uv run pytest -q --tb=short tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py -v
2 passed in 0.73s
```

**Non-UTF-8 nit** — a file with an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence fails cleanly, naming the file, instead of raising an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError`:
```
AssertionError: ... tests\test_zzz_mutation_badencoding.py: could not decode as UTF-8 to scan for hand-rolled DDL ('utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 15: invalid start byte)
```

All mutation temp files were deleted before committing; `git status --porcelain` showed only `tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py` changed.

**Targeted suites** (sessions / post-mortem / worktree / worker / worker-health) all pass on the pushed head:
```
uv run pytest tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py tests/test_post_mortem.py tests/test_worktree.py tests/test_worker.py tests/test_worker_health.py
183 passed in 40.22s
```

Lint/format:
```
uv run ruff check tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py
All checks passed!
uv run ruff format --check tests/test_sessions_db_fixtures.py
1 file already formatted
```

## Risks / uncertain areas

The AST walk matches each string literal's value independently, so DDL assembled at runtime via string concatenation across separate literals or expressions (e.g. `"CREATE TABLE " + "message_nodes"`) would not be caught — this mirrors the same blind spot the #323 `load_state` AST lint accepts for its own pattern, and is out of scope for issue #326, which is specifically about copy-pasted/hand-rolled DDL literals. The check intentionally scopes to `CREATE TABLE` DDL for `message_nodes`, not DML/INSERT, so the existing `INSERT INTO message_nodes` regression test in `test_post_mortem.py` continues to work.
title: test(sessions): guard against hand-rolled message_nodes DDL in tests
